description.narrative: The Customs Modernization Project aims to finance (i) the migration and upgrading of the customs automated data processing system (GAMAS); (ii) the improvement of infrastructure at major customs houses and customs border posts; and (iii) institutional strengthening, including business process reengineering, capacity building in relation to the above two components, interagency coordination, regional cooperation, and public-private partnerships.

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 2. Improvement of infrastructure at selected major customs houses and customs border posts, including provision of inspection and laboratory apparatus. Indicator: • Number of online customs declarations increased from 50% before project completion to 90 % by project completion Progress/Status: Achieved. Over 90% of declarations were done online through CAIS. Data Source: • PMO quarterly and annual reports • ADB staff review missions • ICTA report • PPR; PPMS • Midterm review report Baseline value: 90 Baseline value: 90 Target year: 2011 Target value: 90

Output: 3. Institutional strengthening, comprising business process reengineering, capacity building, interagency coordination, regional cooperation, and public-private partnership. Indicator: • Establishment of central data warehouse by project completion Progress/Status: Completed. MCGA Data Center became operational in July 2010. The disaster recovery system was set-up and become operational on 18 May 2011. Baseline value: Y Baseline value: Y Target year: 2010 Target value: Y

Output: Indicator Indicator: • 100 customs officers trained with modernized customs environment Progress/Status: 2,653 officials have been trained. Data Source: • PMO quarterly / annual reports • ADB staff review missions • Reports and manuals by consultants Target year: 2011 Target value: 100

Output: Indicator Indicator: • 50% reduction in the time needed for customs inspection and clearance (compared with before the infrastructure improvements) by project completion Progress/Status: With the improvement of customs house infrastructure and the MON-PRC joint customs control project, the time for customs clearance has been on decline. Time for import clearance has been reduced to 23 minutes from the previous 3 hours (800%); and time for export clearance has been reduced from 140 minutes to about 13 minutes. Data Source: • Incidences of smuggling and drug trafficking captured and compiled by the customs • Surveys of customs performance Baseline value: 50 Baseline value: 50 Target year: 2011 Target value: 50

Output: Indicator Indicator: • 60% reduction in the amount of time needed for customs laboratory analysis results (including cross-city transport) by project completion (compared with before the project) Progress/Status: Technical capacity in laboratory analysis has been enhanced with the newly installed x-ray and other laboratory equipment. Time needed for lab analysis has been reduced by more than 60%. Data Source: • PMO quarterly and annual reports • ADB staff review missions • PPR, PPMS • Midterm review report Baseline value: 60 Baseline value: 60 Target year: 2011 Target value: 60

Output: Indicator Indicator: • Client satisfaction to exceed 80% by project completion Data Source: • MNCCI report and survey • CCC and CAREC reports • Surveys of customs performance • PPR, PPMS, PPER • Midterm review report Target year: 2011 Target value: Y
Output: Indicator Indicator: • Coordination with SSIA and MASM improved Progress/Status: These agencies were active members of PSC. Target year: 2011 Target value: Y

Output: Indicator Indicator: • Manual of reengineered business processes printed and circulated to customs officers Progress/Status: Detailed user manuals were distributed to customs officers and business users. Target year: 2011 Target value: Y

Output: Indicator Indicator: • Participation by the private sector in project implementation and expansion of the customs-business partnership Progress/Status: Business users were consulted during the design of CAIS. Target year: 2011 Target value: Y

Output: Indicator Indicator: • Procedures harmonized and data exchanged in customs cooperation with neighboring countries Progress/Status: MON-PRC Joint Customs Control started pilot operation in December 2009. Expansion of JCC to one more pair of Border Crossing Points on 15 November 2011. Target year: 2011 Target value: Y
